doc.title: Mike Wofford interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 13, 1998

title: Hearing Gerry Mulligan's tentet and becoming absorbed in jazz
summary: A high school classmate played him the Mulligan tentet album, the day he went from mild interest to total absorption.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: But that was pretty radical stuff, even in the ‘40s and early ‘50s. But I heard through a classmate, actually I played trombone in the school band at the high school, here at Point Loma High School, and the trombonist I sat next to, another kid my age, we were probably in about the tenth grade, had bought an LP. By this time there were ten inch LPs. And he said you’ve got to come over and hear this record I bought. And so I went by his house after school and it was Gerry Mulligan’s tentet album, which is I think a classic recording, it was on I think Capitol Records and this would have been around 1953 or 4, probably ‘54, and it had Chet Baker and Art Pepper and a great L.A. band, and of course all of Gerry Mulligan’s writing. And as I discovered a few years later when I became a little more knowledgeable, it was really all pretty much out of the Gil Evans/Miles Davis collaboration records. They were originally 45s I think. But I wasn’t aware of them yet, and to me this was just breathtaking music, which it still holds up really well, if you’re familiar with that album. So anyway the writing and the instrumentation, Gerry was using French horn and tuba and the colors and the swing, the time feel, the freedom in the soloing, the whole thing, I always remember that day as the day that I went from being maybe mildly interested in the music to being absolutely absorbed with it.

I love to hear those little moments in a person’s life that really make a difference. And if you hadn’t sat down next to that fellow that day or whatever, or if he hadn’t brought that record, things might have been different.
Well he was much hipper than I was because he had the record, I didn’t.
Did you go get your own copy?
